extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (junior and supervisory examiners, SPEs, trainers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for conducting patent examination at the USPTO, including search, claim interpretation, office action drafting, docket management, production metrics, and quality indicia. Intended to train examiners how to evaluate patentability and produce clear, compact prosecution records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production (examiner work metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Production is a metric for the amount of work that an examiner performs in a specified amount of examining time, based on variables such as the Office action count value, expectancy of each application examined, and the examiner’s position factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office action count values range between zero and two. The expectancy of an application is based on the complexity of the subject matter and can vary considerably. The examiner’s position factor is based on experience level (GS/grade). Production measures should reflect these variables when assessing output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket management (timeliness and flow)
rubrics_metrics.description: Docket management provides an objective measure of the timeliness and flow of patent applications through the examination process in accordance with prescribed time periods set by USPTO policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the USPTO: completes examination within statutory time periods. For the applicant: promotes compact prosecution. Docket management is evaluated by whether applications progress through required milestones and statutory deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with statutes, rules, and case law (quality core)
rubrics_metrics.description: Office action quality is evaluated based on the extent of compliance with applicable statutes, rules, and case law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must ensure legal bases (e.g., 35 U.S.C. §§ 101, 102, 103, 112) are correctly applied and cited. Legal and procedural compliance is a primary determinant of quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and prior art indicia
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s search and the prior art found encompass the inventive concept as defined in the disclosure for the examined invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance may be demonstrated when office actions or prosecution histories include some or all exemplary activities (thorough search, appropriate use of classifications, combination of text/classification searches). See MPEP 904.02 guidance on search completeness and prioritization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of the record indicia
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s written prosecution record promotes clarity of the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office actions and prosecution histories, taken as a whole, should make the issues, findings of fact, and legal bases clear. Clarity aids applicant understanding and promotes efficient prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact prosecution indicia
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s written prosecution record promotes compact prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office actions should be structured to minimize unnecessary cycles, anticipate applicant responses, and clearly narrow issues to promote efficient resolution of patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biweek planning and prioritization
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize by making a list of applications that must be completed for the current biweek (e.g., oldest new case, amended cases, special new cases, expedited cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other permitted activities during the biweek include training, meetings with SPE/primary about cases (search strategy), and calling applicants for restrictions or interviews. Planning should balance production goals and necessary non-examining tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-examination considerations (classification, routing, restriction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before examination, determine whether the application has been properly classified and routed and whether the application should be restricted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper classification affects the field(s) to be searched and examiner assignment; restriction decisions should be made early to shape effective prosecution and search strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the invention and determine claim scope
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner should understand the invention based on the claims and the specification; an examiner cannot search effectively without understanding the inventive concept or scope of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take notes on key concepts and/or diagram the claims. Check for claim interpretation issues: determine the broadest reasonable interpretation in light of the specification and ensure proper weight is given to claim limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete and thorough search (MPEP guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete and thorough search enables an examiner to get the most pertinent art as early as possible; a text search alone is rarely sufficient and should be combined with other criteria (e.g., classification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize areas most likely to yield relevant prior art. A proper field of search normally includes the classification locations where the claimed subject matter would be properly classified at the time of classification or grant (MPEP 904.02 and 904.02(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary search activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended preliminary searches include inventor name searching, assignee name searching, citation or patent family searching, and product/press release searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the IDS for classification clues in cited references; see what art was applied or filed in the U.S. or elsewhere; look for foreign search reports. Note: 'applicant' can encompass inventor and assignee (37 CFR 1.42).

rubrics_metrics.name: When to start searching
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin searching when the examiner understands the invention and the claim limitations and the broadest reasonable interpretation in light of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not undertake a search until the inventive concept and claim scope are clear enough to craft an effective search strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to search (search strategy construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft a search strategy by considering relevant CPC maingroups/subgroups, relevant keywords/synonyms/phrases, related groups/keywords, and the most active areas for the application (foreign art & NPL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a combination of classification and text searches and prioritize CPC locations and keywords most likely to contain pertinent art.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to stop searching
rubrics_metrics.description: Stop searching after completely executing the search strategy, after searching for all claimed limitations and potential reasonably expected limitations, and after assessing whether the art can be easily overcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1) & 102(b)(2) exceptions (same applicant) apply. Evaluate whether the art reads on the inventive concept (not just the words of the claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use available resources to overcome roadblocks
rubrics_metrics.description: When encountering roadblocks, consult other examiners, Quality Enhancement Meetings (QEM), the Scientific and Technical Information Center (STIC), or reach out to other technology areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage institutional resources and peer consultation to improve search results, interpretations, or legal analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to make a rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Before making a rejection, determine whether it is applied under the proper statute (35 U.S.C. §§ 101, 102, 103, 112), whether it is legally and technically proper, whether it will clarify the record, and whether an examiner’s amendment would place the claims in condition for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject only when statute and facts support it, it helps clarify record issues, and after considering the impact of potential examiner amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance decision criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine if a claim is allowable, ensure all relevant searches are completed, ensure no claim limitations are characterized in the specification as known or conventional, compare reasons for allowance against the strongest rejection, and consult supervisor/trainer as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowance should be based on thorough search and legal analysis; consultation is recommended when in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support findings of fact with documentary evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence is the collection of information intended to convince as to a fact; documentary evidence is generally needed to support findings of fact. Patent examiners are the 'fact finders.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document search results, references relied on, factual bases for rejections or allowances, and any relied-upon non-patent literature or product evidence to support the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formation of an Office action — statutory checks
rubrics_metrics.description: When forming an Office action, examine whether the claimed invention meets statutory requirements: 35 U.S.C. 101, support in specification per 35 U.S.C. 112(a), definiteness per 35 U.S.C. 112(b), novelty under 35 U.S.C. 102, and non-obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each statutory point should be expressly considered and addressed in the Office action where relevant; failures must be explained with factual and legal support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action drafting quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Office actions should properly communicate the basis for a rejection so that issues can be identified early and the applicant can be given fair opportunity to reply. They should anticipate applicant questions and be clear and concise (MPEP 2142).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft office actions to identify issues, explain reasoning, cite supporting references/statutes, and anticipate likely applicant responses to promote compact prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action posting and supervisory review
rubrics_metrics.description: After a junior examiner completes an Office action, they post it to a primary patent examiner or supervisory patent examiner for review; the reviewing examiner may request changes or make recommendations — an iterative process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize different levels of authority based on grade level; be prepared for iteration and supervisory feedback to improve clarity/legal sufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage non-examining time effectively (interviews, training, meetings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-examining activities include interviews (average 1 per biweek), attending training (average 17 hours per fiscal year, plus additional available time), and staff meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance non-examining activities with production and docket needs; use interviews and training to improve case outcomes and examination quality.
